newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Work starts on power lines linking Iran to Armenia.
newsitem.headline: Work starts on power lines linking Iran to Armenia.

text.p: Repair work on high-voltage electricity lines linking Iran's power grid to Armenia's has begun, and tests on the lines are being run, Armenian Energy Minister Gagik Martirosyan said on Friday.
"Work has begun on repairing and testing the high-voltage power lines, connecting the energy systems of Iran and Armenia," he said, adding the lines were first connected on Wednesday.
After the work was complete, the two countries could begin to exchange electricity, he added.
In its initial stages, the project will allow the landlocked former Soviet republic to receive up to 60 megawatts of energy per day, and that this will gradually increase, he added.
Martirosyan said in February that Armenia produced enough energy to meet domestic demand, but wanted to reduce dependence on its nuclear power plant and on a gas pipeline from Georgia.
"This power line not only ensures the reliability of the electricity grid, but is of strategic significance," said deputy energy minister Karena Galusyana.
"Armenia now has the chance of becoming a transit country, exporting electricity to Georgia and other countries," he said.
